name: "Freezer Friendly" Red Chicken Enchiladas with Cheese, Zucchini & Corn (Batch-Cooking)

instructions.primary_message: This recipe makes 2 (9 x 13-inch) baking pans of enchiladas or 8 servings (4 servings per pan).
FOR THE FILLING: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
2 medium zucchini squash
1 jalapeño pepper
½ small bunch cilantro

instructions.primary_message: Trim and quarter zucchini lengthwise, then cut crosswise into bite-sized pieces. Place in a large bowl.

Quarter jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon to reduce spice level. Small dice and add to the bowl with the zucchini. (Be careful with jalapeños; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Preheat a large pot over medium-high heat.
While the pot heats up, peel, halve, and small dice onion; peel and mince garlic. Add both to the bowl.
Once the pot is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add veggies and spices; cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, 5-6 minutes. (Reserve bowl for the next step.)
instructions.secondary_message:
1 tbsp extra virgin olive oil
1 ½ tsp oregano, dried
1 tsp salt
½ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Meanwhile, shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Place in the reserved bowl and set aside.
When the veggies are softened, add corn to the pot. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until corn is just warmed through, 3-4 minutes.
Transfer cooked veggies to the bowl with the cilantro, along with chicken and cheese, then stir to combine the filling.
instructions.secondary_message:
4 cups cooked chicken (shredded)
shredded cheese, Mexican blend

instructions.primary_message: TO ASSEMBLE THE ENCHILADAS: Coat two 9"x13" disposable foil pans with oil.

Working in batches, warm tortillas in a microwave, oven, or skillet. Place warmed tortillas on a flat surface, then arrange a ⅓-cup of filling down the center of each. Roll up tightly and place, seam-side down, in the pans. Top with enchilada sauce, then sprinkle with additional cheese.
instructions.secondary_message:
4 (10 oz) can red enchilada sauce
shredded cheese, Mexican blend

instructions.primary_message: STORING & BAKING: Tightly cover each pan with aluminum foil, then wrap the whole pan with plastic wrap. Place in the freezer for up to 1 month. HEATING: For best results, bake enchiladas from frozen, removing plastic wrap. Place foil-covered pan(s) in a preheated 375°F oven and bake until filling is heated through and cheese is just melted, 45-50 minutes. Remove the foil and continue to bake until cheese is golden and bubbly, 10 minutes more. Remove from oven and let stand 5 minutes before enjoying! (If you'd prefer to bake directly after assembly, place enchiladas in a preheated 350°F oven, uncovered, and bake until juices bubble and cheese is melted and golden on top, about 40 minutes.)
